# onpager_escalation_chain (Resource)

Manage one team's escalation chain and its complete ordered step definition.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "onpager_escalation_chain" "example" {
  team_id = var.team_id
  name    = "Primary escalation"
  steps = [
    { kind = "notify_user", target_user_id = var.user_id },
    { kind = "wait", wait_seconds = 60 },
    { kind = "notify_channel", channel_sources = ["service", "team"] },
    { kind = "repeat" },
  ]
}

variable "team_id" {
  description = "Existing owning team UUID."
  type        = string
}

variable "user_id" {
  description = "Existing user UUID to notify when this chain runs."
  type        = string
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Nonempty chain name without leading or trailing whitespace. Duplicate names are allowed.
- `steps` (Attributes List) Ordered chain steps; list order defines execution order. An empty list is allowed. Each kind accepts only its applicable settings; omit or use `null` for other settings. Server-generated step IDs are not managed. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--steps))
- `team_id` (String) Owning team UUID. Changing it replaces the chain. Must be a nonzero canonical lowercase UUID.

### Optional

- `off_hours_delegate_chain_id` (String) Explicit off-hours delegation target chain UUID. Omission or `null` removes delegation when the definition is updated. Must be a nonzero canonical lowercase UUID when set.
- `work_calendar_id` (String) Calendar UUID belonging to the owning team. Omission or `null` removes the calendar link when the definition is updated. Must be a nonzero canonical lowercase UUID when set.
- `work_calendar_reference` (String) Calendar evaluation reference: `start_time` (default) or `step_time`. `step_time` requires `work_calendar_id`.

### Read-Only

- `etag` (String) Strong SHA-256 configuration ETag used in `If-Match` for definition replacement and archival. A stale ETag reports a conflict; run a new plan before retrying.
- `id` (String) Stable nonzero canonical lowercase OnPager UUID.

<a id="nestedatt--steps"></a>
### Nested Schema for `steps`

Required:

- `kind` (String) Step kind: `wait`, `repeat`, `notify_user`, `notify_oncall`, `notify_channel`, or `notify_webhook`. `repeat` takes no additional settings.

Optional:

- `channel_sources` (List of String) Nonempty list of unique `team` and/or `service` catalog sources in priority order. Required only for `notify_channel`.
- `importance` (String) Notification importance: `default` or `important`, only for `notify_user` and `notify_oncall`. Omission or `null` selects `default`, including after removing an explicit value. Must be omitted or `null` for other kinds.
- `schedule_id` (String) Schedule UUID. Required only for `notify_oncall`. Must be a nonzero canonical lowercase UUID when set.
- `target_user_id` (String) User UUID. Required only for `notify_user`. Must be a nonzero canonical lowercase UUID when set.
- `wait_seconds` (Number) Whole-second wait duration from 1 through 9223372036. Required only for `wait`; zero is invalid.
- `webhook_id` (String) Webhook UUID. Required only for `notify_webhook`. Must be a nonzero canonical lowercase UUID when set.

## Import

Import using `team_uuid/chain_uuid`. The state `id` contains only the chain
UUID. Archived chains cannot be restored through import.

Use an `import` block:

```terraform
import {
  to = onpager_escalation_chain.example
  id = "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111/44444444-4444-4444-8444-444444444444"
}
```

Or use the CLI:

```shell
terraform import onpager_escalation_chain.example 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111/44444444-4444-4444-8444-444444444444
```

## Lifecycle

Rules, schedules, outgoing webhooks and work calendars referenced by the chain
are managed separately. The API validates ownership, availability and delegation
constraints.

Updates replace the complete definition using the observed strong SHA-256 ETag.
A stale ETag reports a conflict and requires a new plan; the provider does not
retry with a newer ETag.

Destroy archives the chain, preserving its UUID, steps, historical links and
existing runs. Rules, incoming delegation links and current responder or
incident policies can block archival with `chain_in_use`. Remove those
references explicitly; failed archival retains state.

Archived chains remain readable through the API but cannot be updated, restored
or used for new runs. A confirmed archive removes the managed resource from
state; a later apply creates a new UUID. Definitions and ETags persist in state.

## Permissions

Requires owning-team grants `escalation_chains.create`,
`escalation_chains.read`, `escalation_chains.update` and
`escalation_chains.delete`. Service accounts require explicit native grants and
access to referenced configuration.
